extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and computational group theory users of GAP (developers/users constructing pc groups, fp groups, extensions, coset enumerations, and related algorithms)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference guidelines for using GAP functions related to pc groups, group extensions/cohomology, finitely presented groups, coset tables, and associated algorithms. Covers preconditions, return types, options, and caveats for these operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module generator alignment with Pcgs
rubrics_metrics.description: The generators of the module M must correspond to the Pcgs (polycyclic generating sequence) value of the pc group G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many functions (TwoCoboundaries, TwoCocycles, TwoCohomology, etc.) require that the module generators correspond to the Pcgs of G; failure to provide matching ordering/structure can make results meaningless.

rubrics_metrics.name: TwoCoboundaries preconditions and return
rubrics_metrics.description: TwoCoboundaries(G, M) returns the group of 2-coboundaries of a pc group G by the G-module M. The generators of M must correspond to the Pcgs value of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The group of coboundaries is returned as a vector space over the field underlying M; expect the output to be given in terms of vectors over that field.

rubrics_metrics.name: TwoCocycles preconditions and return
rubrics_metrics.description: TwoCocycles(G, M) returns the 2-cocycles of a pc group G by the G-module M. The generators of M must correspond to the Pcgs of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The operation returns a list of vectors over the field underlying M whose additive group generates the group of 2-cocycles; inspect the returned vectors accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: TwoCohomology scope and return
rubrics_metrics.description: TwoCohomology(G, M) computes the second cohomology group for the special case of a pc group G and returns a record defining H^2 as the factor space of cocycles by coboundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G must be a pc group and M's generators must correspond to G's pcgs. The returned record provides linear mappings and vector-space descriptions of the cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions equivalence vs isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions(G, M) returns all extensions of G by the G-module M up to equivalence as pc groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are computed up to equivalence but not up to isomorphism; identical isomorphism types may appear more than once in the returned list. Use ExtensionRepresentatives with a suitable P to reduce by compatible-pairs action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension by cocycle and consistency check
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension(G, M, c) returns the extension defined by cocycle c as a pc group. ExtensionNC does the same but does not check the resulting group for consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ExtensionNC only if you intentionally skip consistency checking; otherwise prefer Extension which validates the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: SplitExtension generality
rubrics_metrics.description: SplitExtension(G, M) returns the split extension of G by the G-module M; M need not be elementary abelian and split extensions of arbitrary pc groups are possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 3-argument variant (SplitExtension(G, aut, N)) exists where aut is a homomorphism from G into Aut(N) for split extensions of pc groups by pc groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: ModuleOfExtension meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: ModuleOfExtension(E) returns the module of an extension E of G by M: the normal subgroup of E corresponding to M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This attribute extracts the subgroup played by the module inside the extension; useful to inspect or reconstruct module structure from an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: CompatiblePairs function and options
rubrics_metrics.description: CompatiblePairs([A,] G, M[, D]) returns the group of compatible pairs of G with the G-module M as a subgroup of Aut(G) × Aut(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aut(M) is treated as subgroup of a general linear group. Optional D restricts to compatible pairs in D; optional A (a group of automorphisms of G) can be supplied to avoid computing full Aut(G).

rubrics_metrics.name: ExtensionRepresentatives under group action
rubrics_metrics.description: ExtensionRepresentatives(G, M, P) returns all extensions of G by M up to equivalence under the action of P, where P is a subgroup of the group of compatible pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to compute extensions up to equivalence induced by automorphisms (compatible pairs) to eliminate redundancies due to that action.

rubrics_metrics.name: PcGroup code validity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PcGroupCode(code, size) returns a pc group corresponding to code and size; the argument code must be a valid code for a pcgs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid codes are usually obtained from CodePcgs or CodePcGroup. If an invalid code is supplied, behavior is undefined ('anything may happen').

rubrics_metrics.name: RandomIsomorphismTest inputs and probabilistic guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: RandomIsomorphismTest(coderecs, n) expects coderecs to be records with components code and order (describing groups via PcGroupCode); n is a non-negative integer controlling the probability of detecting isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n = 0 nothing is done. Larger n increases the probability of finding all isomorphisms but the probabilistic method cannot guarantee to find all isomorphisms for any finite n.

rubrics_metrics.name: FpGroup representation caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: While every finite group can be represented as an FpGroup, it is usually more efficient to work in other representations (e.g., pc groups or permutation groups) for many computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For higher-level computations like conjugacy classes or character tables, prefer IsomorphismPcGroup or IsomorphismPermGroup; many FpGroup computations may be slow or non-terminating unless the group is known to be finite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifying relations vs equations when creating FpGroups
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating an FpGroup from a free group, relations may be given either as a list of relators (words) or as a list of equations (pairs of words), but the two methods cannot currently be mixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use F / rels or the infix operator / consistently; mixing relators and equations is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generator names are display-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Names displayed for generators are not variables; to access generators by name you must introduce variables and assign the group's generators to them (or use AssignGeneratorVariables interactively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect 'a' or 'b' shown in prints to be display labels; attempting to use them as variables without assignment raises errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality test may not terminate
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing equality of two elements in an FpGroup (\=) may take a very long time and cannot be guaranteed to finish because of undecidability in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP's method: try bounded Todd-Coxeter to find a faithful permutation representation, then Knuth-Bendix rewriting systems; if comparing elements in a subgroup, consider translating the problem into a new FpGroup by rewriting (IsomorphismFpGroup) or use kbmag package. Be prepared for warnings, long runtimes, or nontermination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total ordering of FpGroup elements is not stable across runs
rubrics_metrics.description: The < ordering for FpGroup elements depends on the method chosen by GAP and is not guaranteed reproducible across different runs or different constructions of the same syntactic presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only guarantee: ordering stays the same for one family during its lifetime. Use the attribute FpElmComparisonMethod(fam) to obtain the comparison function used.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetReducedMultiplication tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: SetReducedMultiplication(obj) forces immediate reduction when multiplying elements of an FpGroup, keeping words short at extra cost per multiplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when shorter representative words are important and you accept increased overhead per multiplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: FreeGenerators/Relators attributes only for full FpGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: FreeGroupOfFpGroup, FreeGeneratorsOfFpGroup, and RelatorsOfFpGroup are attributes available only for the full finitely presented group (not arbitrary subgroups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction of subgroups of index 1 may produce a subgroup object distinct from the whole group; use Parent to retrieve the full group.

rubrics_metrics.name: UnderlyingElement and ElementOfFpGroup usage
rubrics_metrics.description: UnderlyingElement(elm) returns the representative word from the free group used for an FpGroup element; ElementOfFpGroup(fam, word) creates an element in the FpGroup from a word in the underlying free generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to convert between printed/displayed elements and their underlying free-group word representatives; helps avoid confusion about whether an object is a word or a group element.

rubrics_metrics.name: FpGroup operations may require coset enumeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Many methods for finitely presented groups rely on coset enumeration; operations like IsomorphismPermGroup may attempt to obtain a faithful permutation representation but might run long or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If HasIsFinite is unknown, some functions may error rather than trigger expensive IsFinite tests automatically; be mindful of potential long-running enumerations and resource constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: PseudoRandom for FpGroups: use radius option
rubrics_metrics.description: The default PseudoRandom algorithm produces extremely long words for finitely presented or free groups; specify radius to get words in the ball of given radius with roughly equal distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call PseudoRandom(g: radius := l) to obtain reasonable-length words sampled from the ball of radius l.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetTable structure and computation
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetTable(G, H) returns the coset table (permutation representation on cosets of H) as a list of generator lists; computed by Todd-Coxeter coset enumeration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generator lists correspond to generators and inverses; apply PermList to generator lists to obtain permutations. Performance can be influenced by global variables CosetTableDefaultLimit and CosetTableDefaultMaxLimit and options to CosetTableFromGensAndRels.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetTableFromGensAndRels options: max and silent
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetTableFromGensAndRels(fgens, grels, fsgens) is the internal Todd-Coxeter driver; it accepts options max (limit of cosets) and silent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If enumeration exceeds max, an error is raised and the user is prompted whether to continue unless silent is true (in which case fail is returned). The default max is controlled by CosetTableDefaultMaxLimit.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetTableDefaultMaxLimit behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetTableDefaultMaxLimit is the default limit for the number of cosets allowed in coset enumeration (default 4096000). If reached, GAP issues an error and prompts to continue or stop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting the limit to 0 or infinity disables the safety stop and allows enumeration until exhaustion of resources. Hitting the limit may enter a break-loop with options to continue with a larger limit or quit.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetTableDefaultLimit and memory tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetTableDefaultLimit is the default number of cosets with which a coset table is initialized (default 1000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set it to a number expected to be sufficient for subsequent enumerations; too small may cause extensions (expensive), too large wastes space. Adjust based on expected subgroup indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generator selection heuristics
rubrics_metrics.description: MostFrequentGeneratorFpGroup(G) returns a generator that occurs most frequently in relators; IndicesInvolutaryGenerators(G) returns indices of generators known to be involutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These internal heuristics are used to improve performance of coset enumeration and other algorithms; knowledge about involutions can speed enumeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization of coset tables (lenlex vs semilenlex)
rubrics_metrics.description: A coset table is standardized if the words representing cosets are length-plus-lexicographically ordered (lenlex). GAP's default standard is "lenlex" but the older "semilenlex" remains available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set CosetTableStandard to "lenlex" or "semilenlex" to change convention; use StandardizeTable(table, standard) to (re)standardize a table in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: CosetTableInWholeGroup and Try variant semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetTableInWholeGroup(H) is equivalent to CosetTable(G, H) where G is the unique FpGroup containing H; TryCosetTableInWholeGroup does the same but does not override the silent option and will store a non-fail result in the attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TryCosetTableInWholeGroup when you want a coset table only if it is not too expensive; it will not force interactive prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Augmented coset tables: mutability and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: AugmentedCosetTableInWholeGroup(H[, gens]) returns an augmented coset table for subgroup H. It is mutable so entries may be added but existing entries may not be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gens is given it will be a subset of the primary and secondary subgroup generators. Any entries added must correspond to the subgroup only and not to a homomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Augmented coset table construction methods
rubrics_metrics.description: AugmentedCosetTableMtc and AugmentedCosetTableRrs are internal functions applying Modified Todd-Coxeter (MTC) and Reduced Reidemeister–Schreier (RRS) methods respectively to construct augmented coset tables for subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions accept options such as max and silent similar to CosetTableFromGensAndRels; they are used by subgroup presentation functions (chapter 48.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: RewriteWord behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: RewriteWord(aug, word) rewrites word (a word in the underlying free group) in the subgroup generators given by augmented coset table aug and returns a Tietze-type word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the word is not contained in the subgroup, RewriteWord returns fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low index subgroup computation
rubrics_metrics.description: LowIndexSubgroupsFpGroupIterator(G[, H], index[, excluded]) and LowIndexSubgroupsFpGroup compute representatives of conjugacy classes of subgroups of G containing H with index <= index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions enumerate low index subgroups; be aware of computational cost as index grows.
